images.filename: Sea Cliffs at Porth Dinllaen - geograph.org.uk - 62238.jpg
images.caption: Sea Cliffs at Porth Dinllaen. These are typical 'bay' cliffs for the Llŷn peninsula, comprised of terminal glacial moraine lodged between hard rock headlands. Like the rest of Llŷn these cliffs are eroding, but because of Porth Dinllaen's sheltered aspect erosion here is not as severe as in some locations.
images.alt: Sea Cliffs at Porth Dinllaen. These are typical 'bay' cliffs for the Llŷn peninsula, comprised of terminal glacial moraine lodged between hard rock headlands. images.filename: Taith Gerdded Brotest - Protest March - geograph.org.uk - 691561.jpg
images.caption:
Taith Gerdded Brotest - Protest March Between 11 and 14 February 2008 members of Cymdeithas yr Iaith Gymraeg (The Welsh Language Society) marched from Ysgol Y Parc in Bala to Ysgol Llidiardau in Rhoshirwaun to protest against Gwynedd Council's plans to close or federate primary schools in the county. The march was named "O Benllyn i Ben-Llŷn" (From Penllyn - the area around Bala - to Pen-Llŷn - the Llŷn Peninsula).
Along the way they were joined by local parents and children.
Here they are leaving Criccieth on their way to Ysgol Llanystumdwy - the school Lloyd George attended as a boy, now threatened with closure.

The banner reads "Cau Ysgol - Lladd Cymuned" - "Close a School - Kill a Community".

images.caption: Aberdaron - Traeth/Beach Aberdaron stands on the shore of Bae Aberdaron in a small valley at the confluence of the Afon Daron and Afon Cyll-y-felin, between the headlands of Uwchmynydd to the west, and Trwyn y Penrhyn to the east.  At the mouth of the bay stand two islands, Ynysoedd Gwylanod, composed of Ynys Gwylan-fawr and Ynys Gwylan-fach.  The Llŷn Peninsula is a marine eroded platform, an extension of the Snowdonia massif, with a complex geology including Precambrian rocks.  The coastline is rocky, with crags, screes and low cliffs; heather covered hills are separated by valleys occupied by pastures.

images.caption: Cricieth/Criccieth - Min-y-Traeth Cricieth/Criccieth is located in Eifionydd on the Cardigan Bay shore of the Llŷn Peninsula. The town is south facing and built around the rocky outcrop containing Castell Cricieth/Criccieth Castle, which effectively divides the shoreline in two at this point.  The East Shore has a sandy beach with a shallow area for bathing.

Blaenau Ffestiniog railway station - On the left of the picture, Arriva Trains Wales British Rail Class 153 DMU 153327 stands at the standard gauge platform for a Conwy Valley Line service. Note also the different platform heights for the different gauges.
